title: ARBA2GO issue:GO:0016491	 oxidoreductase activity IEA with ARBA00028747  & IPR003462

author: Antonialock
body: oxidoreductase comes from funfam family 3.40.50.720:FF:000311 where there are [two plant proteins](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb?query=%28xref%3A%22funfam-3.40.50.720%3AFF%3A000311%22%29+AND+%28go_manual%3A0016491%29) annotated to (children of) oxidoreductase activity Interestingly SARD4 arabidopsis is annotated to NOT cyclodeaminase activity. For fungi I found a paper on candida parapsilopsis: * Novel imine reductase from yeast Candida parapsilosis purified and characterized. * CpIM1 belongs to unexplored Ornithine cyclodeaminase/Mu crystallin protein family "The OCD-Mu protein family consists of oxidoreductases acting on carbon-nitrogen bonds, which are widely distributed and contain proteins with diverse functions. Mammalian KIREDs, plant and archaeal PipC/PyrC REDs reduce cyclic imino acids, some of which have been explored for the biocatalytic synthesis of chiral N-alkyl amino acids" "cyclodeaminases from several gram-negative bacteria catalyze concerted oxidative-deamination cyclization and reduction of ornithine/lysine" ..."The residues Glu56 (Glu63) and Asp228 (Asp236) from (bacterial) SpLCD (PpOCD), which are considered critical for cyclodeaminase activity are not conserved in CpIM1, plant and mammalian OCD homologs"..."Instead, the position occupied by Asp228 in SpLCD is occupied by serine in all the mammalian OCD homologs which is also suitably positioned to act as a proton donor. In CpIM1, this position is occupied by bulky tyrosine" I aligned these two residues in 2 bacteria, pombe, cerevisiae and human CRYM: so oxidoreductase looks ok as a prediction, from the imine reductase activity of the candida protein? What do you think? I'll put the candida paper on my list to curate

author: sarach06
body:
Hi,
Thank you very much for this. I added oxidoreductase activity to the Family entry IPR003462, which will be available in InterPro 108.0. IPR023401 Is a Homologous superfamily entry to which we try to avoid adding terms, and it refers to the N-terminal domain, that from the description, it "is responsible for substrate binding. This is a dimerisation domain of alanine dehydrogenase and CRYM".
Best wishes,
Sara

author: Antonialock
body: @sarach06 Apologis if I am misunderstanding the workflow but it looks like that interpro includes bacterial proteins? I don't think the bacterial enzymes are oxidoreductases, bacterial Ornithine cyclodeaminase/mu-crystallin are ec 4.3.1.12

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Antonia,
Yes, you are right! My bad, I got carried away with your first message. Thanks for replying! I removed the term so it doesn't propagate to that set of proteins. I won't add any other term as it won't fit all the members.

Best wishes,
Sara
